DEMOG 501: This course introduces graduate students to the foundations of formal demography and social demography.
DEMOG 510: This course is a seminar series focused on demographic processes, such as fertility, family transitions, migration, aging, and mortality.
DEMOG 520: This course is a seminar series focused on the consequences of demographic change for societies, population subgroups, communities, households and individuals, as well as how demographic characteristics and processes interact with biological, psychological, behavioral, social, cultural, economic, policy, and/or spatial processes to affect individual, group, and population outcomes.
DEMOG 530: This course is a seminar series focused on advanced research methods used in demographic research.
DEMOG 590: Continuing seminars which consist of a series of individual lectures by faculty, students, or outside speakers.
DEMOG 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, which are superivsed on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
DEMOG 801: This course examines fundamental concepts and ideas in Demography, and U.S. and world population trends associated with these concepts.
DEMOG 802: This course provides an overview of key demographic data sets, and promotes familiarity with, and appropriate use of, these data.
DEMOG 803: This course provides an overview of applications in applied demography in business, non-profit organizations, public policy, and health; including a focus on international applications.
DEMOG 804: This course provides a broad coverage of business demography questions that draw upon knowledge, data, and methods associated with applied demography.
DEMOG 805: This course provides an analysis of selected public sector, non-profit, and public policy demography issues that draw upon knowledge, data, and methods associated with applied demography.
DEMOG 806: This course provides an overview of data, methods, and techniques in applied demography used to help address public health questions.
DEMOG 807: This course provides an overview of applications in small areas population estimation techniques used in public policy, business and academia, including case studies from the United States and other international programs.
DEMOG 808: Students will utilize methods acquired during their program and apply them in a Capstone This is a Capstone course and a requirement for all students in the M.P.S.
